We confirm what is behind your walls before quoting rather than after demolition. Does Avondale's hard water affect a kitchen remodel? Yes, in small ways that add up. The city's 2022 water quality report averaged about 21 grains per gallon for city-produced water — &ldquo;very hard&rdquo; on the report's own scale. That shows up as white spotting on faucets, sinks and dark countertops, scale in aerators, dishwashers and ice makers, and etching on marble. We favor quartz, granite or porcelain around the sink, recommend faucets that handle hard water , and can leave space and plumbing for a water softener or under-sink filtration. Permits & Inspections Kitchen Remodel Permits in Avondale Avondale runs its own permitting. Plan review, permits and inspections go through the Building Services Division of the city's Development Services Department at 11465 W. Civic Center Dr., and applications are filed online through the city's Accela portal. Nothing routes through Maricopa County. Avondale's code says painting, tiling, cabinets and countertops need no building permit, so replacing cabinets and counters inside the existing footprint is the lightest version of the job. Plumbing, electrical, gas and HVAC work beyond minor repairs is not exempt: moving the sink or dishwasher, adding an island sink, running new circuits for countertop receptacles or a dedicated appliance, or extending a gas line for a range. The moment a wall opens up or the panel needs work, the scope and the review both grow, and rough plumbing and wiring are inspected before the walls are closed. We pull the permit, schedule the inspections and meet the inspector ourselves. You should not be the one learning a municipal submittal process in the middle of your own remodel — and a contractor who suggests skipping the permit on a job that needs one is telling you something useful about how they work. If your home is in an HOA, check its rules as well; the city does not track HOA covenants. More detail: Avondale remodeling permits . Home / Services / Kitchen Remodeling / Outdoor Kitchens Outdoor Kitchen Builder Avondale, AZ Outdoor Kitchen Design & Build in Avondale, AZ Get a Free Site Visit Call 602-885-6998 Outdoor Kitchen Builder Avondale, AZ Designed for Avondale's Desert Climate Avondale sits in the low Sonoran Desert at about 1,000 feet. Summers are hot — National Weather Service 1991–2020 normals for the area put the July average high near 106°F, with roughly 111 days a year at 100°F or above — but the cooler months from October through April are prime time for cooking and eating outside, and a well-shaded patio stays usable on summer evenings too. Whether you want a simple grill station for weekend barbecues or a fully equipped outdoor kitchen complete with a refrigerator, prep sink, bar seating, and covered shade structure, Infinity Kitchens and Baths designs and builds it, starting with a free site visit at your Avondale home. Our outdoor kitchens are built to match the same quality standards we apply to every indoor kitchen remodeling project. That means proper structural framing, weatherproof materials selected specifically for Avondale's low-desert heat, sun, and monsoon storms, professional gas and plumbing rough-in, and countertops and cabinetry that will still look sharp five years from now. We are not a specialty outdoor-only company — we are a full-service design-build contractor, which means your outdoor kitchen integrates seamlessly with any interior work happening at the same time. Every project begins with a free site visit where we measure your patio or yard, discuss your cooking and entertaining habits, and sketch a preliminary layout on the spot. From there our team produces a CAD floor plan and 3D rendering so you can see exactly what you are getting before a single block is laid. We manage City of Avondale permits, subcontractors, and scheduling — you stay informed without being buried in logistics. What We Build in Your Outdoor Kitchen From a standalone grill island to a full outdoor cooking suite, here are the core components we design, source, and install. Built-In Grill Station We install gas, charcoal, and kamado-style grills set into a stone or stucco surround. Built-in grills eliminate the propane tank shuffle and give your outdoor kitchen a clean, permanent look. We can add side burners, rotisserie access, and smoker boxes as part of the same island build. Outdoor Countertops We work with granite, porcelain slab, and cast concrete — all UV-stable, non-porous options that stand up to direct Arizona sun without fading or cracking. The right outdoor countertop pairs with your indoor countertop material choices and looks intentional rather than afterthought. Outdoor Cabinetry Standard wood cabinets will warp and rot within a single monsoon season. We specify marine-grade polymer or 304-grade stainless steel cabinetry for every outdoor kitchen — materials engineered for moisture, UV, and temperature swings. You get the storage convenience of an indoor kitchen without the maintenance headache. Refrigeration & Ice Outdoor-rated refrigerator drawers, undercounter beverage centers, ice makers, and kegerator taps keep drinks and ingredients cold without trips back inside. We install only appliances rated for outdoor ambient temperatures — a critical distinction since standard indoor refrigerators will fail prematurely when exposed to heat and UV. Outdoor Sink & Plumbing A dedicated prep sink cuts down on kitchen traffic and makes outdoor entertaining far more convenient. We run supply lines and a waste drain to your island, with the option for hot-and-cold or cold-only depending on your site's plumbing proximity and budget. Avondale's water is very hard — the city's 2022 water quality report averaged about 21 grains per gallon for city-produced water — so we specify faucets with replaceable cartridges and plan for filtration on any ice maker or refrigerator line. Covered Patio & Pergola In full summer sun, shade is what keeps an outdoor kitchen usable from late spring into fall. We integrate pergolas, solid patio covers, and shade sails directly into the kitchen design so the structure and the cooking station feel like one cohesive space rather than separate projects bolted together over time. Patio covers go through City of Avondale permitting with their own final inspection, and we build that into the schedule. Outdoor Kitchen Materials That Survive Avondale Weather An outdoor kitchen here faces extreme heat (about 21 days a year at 110°F or hotter in National Weather Service 1991–2020 normals), intense UV, monsoon dust and downpours, and very hard water. Material choices have to hold up under all of those stressors at once. Countertop Materials Granite is the classic outdoor choice for good reason: it weathers exceptionally well, handles thermal shock without cracking, and a properly sealed slab will last decades outdoors. We recommend a penetrating sealer reapplication every two to three years in full Arizona sun, and a lighter color for any slab without shade — dark granite gets very hot to the touch in summer. Porcelain slab is our first recommendation for low-maintenance clients. It is UV-immune by nature — the color is fired into the body of the tile, not applied as a coating — and its virtually zero water absorption rate means hard-water spots, monsoon dust, and grill grease stay on the surface and wipe off instead of soaking in. Large-format porcelain slabs (12mm or thicker) give you a seamless, contemporary look that is extremely popular in current outdoor kitchen builds. Cast concrete can be a beautiful outdoor countertop material when mixed and sealed correctly, but it requires an experienced installer. An improperly cured or under-reinforced concrete top will develop hairline cracks under the thermal stress of full desert sun, and an unsealed top will soak up hard-water minerals and grease. We use fiber-reinforced mixes and apply quality penetrating sealers when concrete is specified. Structure & Cabinet Materials Stucco over metal stud framing is the most common outdoor kitchen structure in Arizona for good reason — it is fast to build, durable, and can be colored and textured to match your home's exterior perfectly. The metal stud interior will not rot or warp in Arizona's dry heat, and stucco sheds monsoon rain efficiently. CMU block (concrete masonry unit) construction adds mass and permanence for larger projects or when the outdoor kitchen is a freestanding structure well away from the house. Block builds take longer and cost more but offer unmatched structural rigidity and fire resistance around the grill area. Cabinetry in an outdoor kitchen should never be standard wood. Our go-to choices are marine-grade HDPE polymer, which looks like painted wood but has zero water uptake, or 304-grade stainless steel with brushed or powder-coated finishes. Both options carry lifetime warranties against delamination, warping, and corrosion. For homeowners who want to complement a broader renovation, these same durable principles inform our approach to whole house remodeling projects where exterior-facing spaces are involved. Permit & HOA note: Avondale's building code does not name outdoor kitchens specifically, but new gas piping and new electrical circuits are not on the city's permit-exempt list, so an island with a built-in gas grill or new outlets needs a permit from the City of Avondale Building Services Division. The city also does not track HOA covenants and tells owners to check with their HOA before applying for a permit. If your neighborhood has an HOA, get its approval for the structure, finishes, and location first — the CAD plan we prepare is a good starting point for that submittal. Popular Outdoor Kitchen Layouts The right layout depends on your patio dimensions, how you cook, and how many people you typically entertain. Here are the three configurations we build most often. L-Shape Outdoor Kitchen The L-shape is the most popular layout we build. One leg of the L holds the grill and high-heat appliances, while the second leg extends into a prep counter and bar-height seating for guests. The layout creates a natural social zone — the cook faces guests rather than a wall — and fits efficiently on most standard patio spaces. An L-shaped island typically requires a patio of at least 12 feet in one direction. Linear / Straight Run When the patio is narrow — a long side yard or a covered lanai with limited depth — a straight-run island is the most space-efficient choice. All appliances, the sink, and counter space line up along a single island that can span anywhere from 8 to 20 feet. Linear layouts also work well as a secondary cooking station alongside an existing pool or spa area where you want the outdoor kitchen to stay visually recessed. U-Shape Entertaining Island The U-shape is the full outdoor entertaining experience. Three sides of counter space create a wraparound bar that seats six or more guests while the cook works the interior of the U. This layout comfortably accommodates a grill, side burner, prep sink, refrigerator, and an outdoor pizza oven in a single integrated structure. U-shape builds require more patio square footage but deliver a truly resort-level outdoor kitchen experience for homeowners who entertain frequently. Explore our full kitchen remodeling capabilities. Explore Kitchen Remodeling Outdoor Kitchen FAQ What's the best countertop material for an outdoor kitchen in Arizona? For most Avondale homeowners we recommend porcelain slab or granite. Porcelain is UV-immune, has near-zero water absorption, and requires the least maintenance of any outdoor countertop option. Granite performs excellently outdoors and adds a natural stone aesthetic — it just needs periodic sealing. For any counter in full sun, pick a lighter color: dark stone gets very hot to the touch in summer. Concrete can be beautiful but requires a skilled installer, proper curing, and good sealing to resist hairline cracking and hard-water staining. Quartz is not recommended outdoors because the resin binders in engineered quartz are vulnerable to UV and will discolor or delaminate over time. Can outdoor kitchens be used year-round in Avondale? Yes, but the seasons work in reverse from most of the country. Avondale is low desert, about 1,000 feet, and National Weather Service 1991–2020 normals for the area show a July average high of about 106°F, roughly 111 days a year at 100°F or hotter, and about 21 days at 110°F or more. October through April is prime outdoor cooking season, with winter lows that average in the 40s. In summer, most people cook early or after sunset, which is why we design for shade, airflow, and good lighting from the start. Monsoon season (officially June 15 to September 30) brings dust storms and sudden downpours, so appliance covers and good drainage around the island matter more here than freeze protection does. How long does outdoor kitchen construction take? A typical outdoor kitchen project runs three to six weeks from start to completion. Countertop fabrication — especially for custom stone or porcelain — adds roughly ten to fourteen days from templating to installation. Projects that include a new concrete pad, a covered patio structure, or extensive utility trenching will run toward the longer end of that range. We provide a detailed project schedule during the proposal phase so you know what to expect week by week. What appliances can I include in an outdoor kitchen? Virtually any appliance that is available in an outdoor-rated version: built-in gas or charcoal grills, kamado cookers, flat-top griddles, side burners, outdoor pizza ovens, undercounter refrigerators, drawer refrigerators, beverage centers, kegerators, outdoor-rated ice makers, warming drawers, and outdoor dishwashers. The key is specifying appliances rated for outdoor ambient temperatures. Standard indoor appliances are not engineered for direct sun, temperature swings, or humidity exposure and will have shortened lifespans and may void their warranties when installed outdoors. Home / Services / Kitchen Remodeling / Small Kitchen Remodeling Small Kitchen Remodeling in Avondale — Maximum Impact, Minimum Space Get a Free Design Consult Call 602-885-6998 Small Kitchen Remodeling in Avondale, AZ Small Kitchen, Big Transformation A small kitchen does not have to feel cramped or dysfunctional. The difference between a kitchen that feels tight and one that feels efficient comes down to three things: layout, storage, and light — not square footage. When every cabinet, every countertop inch, and every light fixture is positioned with intention, a compact kitchen can outperform a much larger one that was never properly planned. At Infinity Kitchens and Baths, we specialize in turning smaller kitchens into spaces that feel open, organized, and genuinely enjoyable to use. Avondale&rsquo;s housing is young — the median home was built in 2002, and most neighborhoods are tract homes from the 1990s and 2000s. Newer does not always mean better planned, though. Many production-built kitchens from those decades were laid out to a builder&rsquo;s budget rather than around how a family actually cooks: short upper cabinets under a dropped soffit, an angled corner sink that eats counter space, a peninsula that pinches the path to the family room. Older homes, including those around Old Town on Western Ave, can have even tighter, closed-off kitchens. Either way, the complaints are the same: galley kitchens that lack natural light, wasted corner cabinet space that nobody can reach, insufficient countertop workspace, and layouts that create traffic jams the moment two people try to cook at the same time. Sound familiar? These are exactly the problems a well-planned small kitchen remodel solves. What makes our approach different is that we do not ask you to imagine the transformation — we show it to you before we ever pick up a demo hammer. Using CAD design software, our team creates a precise digital model of your new kitchen so you can see exactly where the new island will sit, how the cabinets will flow to the ceiling, and how the new lighting will change the feel of the space. By the time we begin work, there are no surprises. If you are ready to explore what is possible, visit our main kitchen remodeling page or call us today for a free in-home consultation. Small Kitchen Design Strategies That Actually Work These are not generic tips from a home magazine — they are the specific moves we make on real kitchen projects to unlock space, improve flow, and bring in more light. Open-Concept Conversion Removing a non-load-bearing wall between the kitchen and living or dining area is often the single highest-impact change you can make. It eliminates the claustrophobic feel of a closed kitchen, floods the space with natural light from adjacent windows, and creates a connected floor plan that feels dramatically larger. We assess the wall structure, handle the City of Avondale permits the work requires, and manage the full conversion from start to finish. Vertical Storage Most small kitchens stop their upper cabinets at eight feet while the ceiling continues to nine or ten. That gap above the cabinets collects dust and wastes valuable storage space. Extending cabinets all the way to the ceiling adds meaningful storage while drawing the eye upward and making the room feel taller. Paired with pull-down shelf systems for the highest cabinets, vertical storage turns wasted air space into practical organization. Light Colors & Reflective Surfaces Color and material choices have a significant psychological effect on perceived space. White and light-toned cabinets reflect ambient light rather than absorbing it, making the room feel brighter and more open. Glossy backsplash tiles bounce light around the room. Glass-front upper cabinet doors break up visual mass while showing off your dishware. These choices cost no more than darker alternatives yet deliver a consistently larger-feeling kitchen. Smart Layout Changes Sometimes a small kitchen simply has the wrong layout. Moving the sink from a wall cabinet to an island, relocating the refrigerator to create a true work triangle, or converting a one-wall kitchen to an L-shape can transform workflow completely. Our design team uses CAD planning to model these changes and verify clearances before any plumbing or electrical work is moved — so the finished layout is functional, not just theoretical. Compact Appliance Options Switching from a 36-inch range to a 30-inch model can free up six inches of counter space — enough to add a meaningful prep area. Counter-depth refrigerators align flush with the cabinet face instead of protruding several inches into the kitchen, which noticeably opens the circulation path. These are small changes that compound quickly in a tight footprint, and they do not require sacrificing cooking performance or refrigerator capacity. Under-Cabinet & Recessed Lighting Dark corners are one of the most common complaints in small kitchens. A single overhead fixture creates shadows on countertops, making the workspace feel smaller and harder to use. Under-cabinet LED strips illuminate the counter surface directly, while recessed ceiling lights eliminate overhead shadows entirely. Layered lighting transforms the visual quality of a small kitchen without changing a single dimension of the space. Choosing the Right Countertop for a Small Kitchen How Color and Material Affect Perceived Space In a small kitchen, the countertop is one of the largest horizontal surfaces the eye lands on, which means its color and material have an outsized effect on how spacious the room feels. Light-colored countertops — white quartz, light gray marble-look porcelain, pale quartzite — reflect natural and artificial light upward, creating an airy, open feel. Darker countertops can certainly be used effectively, but they require more intentional lighting design to avoid making the room feel heavier. There is a practical bonus to going light, too: Avondale&rsquo;s water is very hard — about 21 grains per gallon for city-produced water in the city&rsquo;s 2022 water quality report — and the white mineral spots it leaves around the sink show far less on a light counter than on a dark, polished one. One of the most effective tricks in a small kitchen is matching the backsplash material or color closely to the countertop. When the eye travels along the counter and continues up the wall without a jarring contrast change, the perception of horizontal space extends. A consistent white quartz counter paired with a white subway tile backsplash, for example, reads as one continuous surface rather than two separate elements competing for attention. Visit our custom countertops page to explore the full range of materials we offer. Edge Profiles and Full-Height Slab Backsplash In smaller kitchens, edge profile selection matters more than most homeowners realize. Thick, decorative profiles like ogee or stacked bullnose add visual mass to the edge of the counter, which can make the space feel denser. Eased or pencil-edge profiles keep the counter visually thin and sleek — a better fit for compact footprints where every line should read as clean and simple rather than ornate. For the ultimate in visual continuity, consider a full-height slab backsplash that runs the same stone or quartz material from the countertop all the way up to the upper cabinets. This eliminates the tile grout grid entirely, creates a seamless wall of material, and makes the kitchen feel polished and intentional. It is particularly effective on the range wall where the backsplash has maximum visibility. Our team can walk you through slab backsplash options when you schedule your design consultation. Cabinet Tricks for Small Kitchens Cabinets occupy more visual and physical space in a kitchen than any other element. In a compact kitchen, the right cabinet choices can double your usable storage while simultaneously making the room feel more open. Maximize Storage &rarr; Pull-out shelves in base cabinets: Standard base cabinet shelves waste the back half of the cabinet. Pull-out shelves bring everything within reach and effectively double your usable storage in every base unit. &rarr; Drawer banks instead of doors: Replacing two-door base cabinets with deep drawer stacks gives you organized, visible storage for pots, pans, and dry goods without digging behind doors. &rarr; Lazy Susan in corners: Corner cabinets are notorious dead zones. A well-installed lazy Susan or blind-corner pull-out converts otherwise inaccessible corner space into one of the most-used storage spots in the kitchen. &rarr; Deep drawer utensil organizers: Built-in drawer inserts keep utensils, spices, and small tools sorted and visible. No more rummaging through tangled drawers — everything has a place. &rarr; A sink base planned for filtration: With water as hard as Avondale&rsquo;s, a reverse-osmosis filter or softener loop is a common add-on. We plan the sink base around it from the start, so the equipment does not swallow the only storage under the counter. Maximize Visual Space &rarr; Glass-front upper cabinets: Replacing solid upper cabinet doors with glass fronts breaks up visual mass and creates a sense of depth. The interior becomes part of the design rather than a closed wall. &rarr; Open shelving on one wall: Removing the upper cabinet doors from a single wall section and installing open shelves creates an airy, intentional look while maintaining display and storage functionality. &rarr; Handle-less and integrated pulls: Flush or integrated cabinet pulls create a streamlined, uninterrupted cabinet face. In tight kitchens, eliminating protruding hardware also reduces the chance of catching clothing while navigating the space. &rarr; Cabinet color that blends with walls: Painting cabinets in a color close to the wall color reduces the visual contrast between surfaces, which makes the room read as a unified whole rather than a collection of boxes stacked together. Explore the full range of cabinet styles, finishes, and configurations we offer on our kitchen cabinets page. Small kitchen remodels consistently deliver some of the highest returns on investment in residential remodeling because the kitchen is a central part of daily life and a major factor in home value. What&rsquo;s the best layout for a small galley kitchen? The key is maintaining a clear aisle width of at least 42 inches between the two runs, creating a proper work triangle between the sink, stove, and refrigerator, and ensuring there is adequate countertop space on either side of the range for prep and landing zones. ADA Accessible Bathroom Remodeling Avondale, AZ A Bathroom That Works for Everyone in Your Home ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) guidelines were written for public facilities, but the principles translate powerfully into residential remodeling. For homeowners in Avondale, applying ADA standards to a private bathroom means designing around real human needs: a minimum 60-inch turning radius for wheelchair users, curbless or roll-in showers with no lip to trip over, grab bars anchored to blocking in the wall at precise heights, roll-under sinks and vanities that allow a wheelchair to pull fully underneath, and door openings of at least 32 to 36 inches clear. These are not arbitrary rules — they are dimensions drawn from decades of research into how people with mobility challenges actually use a bathroom safely and independently. In a young, family-heavy city like Avondale, the reasons for an accessible bathroom are usually practical: making room for a parent who is moving in, sharing a house across three generations, recovering from surgery or an injury, supporting a family member with a disability — or simply planning to stay put for the long haul. Planning an accessible bathroom remodel now — rather than retrofitting after a fall or a health event — almost always costs significantly less and delivers a better-integrated result. Blocking can be added behind tile before the walls close up. Structural changes to widen a doorway are far simpler before finish materials go in. The time to act is before you need it, not after. At Infinity Kitchens and Baths, we design accessible bathrooms that look nothing like a hospital room. Frameless glass enclosures on curbless showers look sleek and modern. Teak shower benches read as a spa amenity, not a medical device. Comfort-height toilets are standard in luxury bathrooms. Matte porcelain tile with a slip-resistant coefficient of friction looks beautiful underfoot. Our team has built dozens of fully accessible bathrooms — each one tailored to the homeowner's specific mobility needs, aesthetic preferences, and long-term goals. What We Install ADA Bathroom Features We Install Every accessible bathroom project is different, but these are the core features we design and build for homeowners who need a safer, more functional bathroom. Curbless & Roll-In Showers A zero-threshold shower entry eliminates the biggest trip and transfer hazard in any bathroom. We build curbless showers with properly sloped linear drains so water flows away from the entrance — no lip, no step, no barrier. Roll-in designs are sized to allow full wheelchair access and turning inside the enclosure. Grab Bar Installation (ANSI Compliant) ANSI A117.1 specifies exact placement heights and load ratings for grab bars — horizontal bars at 33–36 inches for toilet transfers, angled bars inside showers for stability while standing or sitting. We install backing (blocking) in the wall framing first, so bars are anchored to hold 250 lbs in any direction, not just drywall. Comfort-Height Toilets Standard toilet bowls sit at 14–15 inches — difficult to rise from for anyone with knee, hip, or lower-back issues. Comfort-height (or ADA-height) toilets measure 17–19 inches from floor to seat rim, dramatically reducing the effort and pain of standing. We pair these with correctly positioned grab bars for a complete transfer solution. Roll-Under Vanities A knee-clearance vanity — open underneath, mounted 27 inches off the floor minimum — allows a wheelchair user to roll directly to the sink and use it comfortably. We insulate exposed plumbing to protect legs from heat, install single-lever faucets within easy reach, and can design floating or furniture-style vanities that look beautiful even without lower cabinet storage. Non-Slip Flooring The CDC reports that more than 235,000 people visit emergency rooms each year for bathroom fall injuries. We specify tile with a dynamic coefficient of friction (DCOF) of 0.42 or greater on wet surfaces — the threshold recommended by the Tile Council of North America for wet areas. Options include matte porcelain, textured natural stone, and luxury vinyl plank with grip surfaces. Wider Doorways & Clearance ADA guidelines call for a minimum 32-inch clear opening (36 inches preferred) and 60 inches of maneuvering clearance in front of the door. We reframe doorways, relocate plumbing or fixtures if necessary, and can replace swing doors with barn-style sliders or offset hinges to recover precious clearance in tighter floor plans. See All Bathroom Remodeling Services Avondale bathrooms vary more than any spec can cover This is the cohort where the standard is most useful as a target and least useful as a promise. A bathroom in a recently built home may already come close on several of the dimensions. A bathroom in one of the city's older houses — Old Town, Cashion and Las Ligas are its oldest neighborhoods — may have a 24-inch door, a room barely five feet wide, and a window exactly where a grab bar wants to go. So we survey before we design. Clear door width measured with the door open, actual floor dimensions rather than plan dimensions, and where the framing and the plumbing actually are. Then we tell you which of the three key figures — the 60-inch turning space (§304.3.1), the 32-inch clear doorway (§404.2.3), the 33-to-36-inch grab bar height (§609.4) — your room can hit and which it cannot. A room that hits two of three honestly is worth more than a room marketed as accessible that hits none. When taking space from next door is the right answer In older houses the bathroom is frequently too small to become genuinely accessible on its own footprint, and the only real fix is to borrow space from an adjacent closet, hallway or bedroom. That is a bigger job with structural and permit implications, and it is not always worth it. But it is the honest option in a room that cannot otherwise take a wheelchair, and we would rather put it on the table than sell you a series of improvements that never quite add up to the outcome you wanted. Where the house has more than one bathroom, converting the better-proportioned one is usually cheaper and better than forcing the primary. When the window, the vent or the slab gets in the way Older bathrooms have a habit of putting something immovable exactly where the design wants to go. A window in the wet wall. A vent stack in the corner you wanted for a bench. A drain that has to move through a concrete slab. None of these are fatal and all of them are cheaper to find during design than during demolition. This is the main reason we survey behind panels and in the attic before producing a number. In a house built on a slab, recessing the floor for a curbless entry or moving a drain means cutting and patching concrete — and if the slab is post-tensioned (the city's inspection codes include post-tension slab inspections), the steel tendons have to be located before anyone cuts. Where a window sits in the shower wall, the usual answers are a glass block infill, a properly flashed and waterproofed replacement unit rated for wet locations, or moving the shower. Which is right depends on the room, and any of them is better than tiling up to a wooden sash and hoping. Permits & Inspections Permits for this work in Avondale Avondale runs Building Services as a division of its own Development Services Department, so plan review, permit issuance and inspections all sit with the city — nothing routes through Maricopa County. The division is at 11465 W. Civic Center Dr. and can be reached at (623) 333-4000; applications are filed online through the city's Accela portal. Since January 1, 2026 the city has enforced the 2024 International Residential Code and the 2023 National Electrical Code, with its own amendments. Avondale's code lets finish work — painting, tiling, cabinets and countertops — go ahead without a building permit, but plumbing, electrical, gas and HVAC work beyond minor repairs is not exempt. Accessibility work touches plumbing and often framing, so it is squarely the kind of job that gets reviewed. Moving a drain, recessing a floor for a curbless entry, or widening a doorway all change things an inspector cares about, and a rebuilt shower gets the city's pre-slope and shower liner test inspections before any tile goes on. We pull the permit and meet the inspector ourselves, and where a scope item isn't clearly on the exempt list, we confirm with Building Services before we start. The ADA standard governs public accommodations, not private homes. Common Questions Accessible Bathroom FAQ What's the difference between ADA and aging-in-place modifications? ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) refers to specific dimensional standards — turning radii, reach ranges, knee clearances — developed primarily for public and commercial facilities. ANSI A117.1 is the corresponding standard applied in residential contexts. "Aging in place" is a broader philosophy: designing a home so a person can remain there safely and comfortably as they age, often without meeting every precise ADA dimension. In practice, many of the features overlap significantly. Our aging-in-place modifications incorporate ADA-derived dimensions wherever they improve safety and usability — the labels are less important than building what actually works for the person who will use the space. Do residential bathrooms have to meet ADA standards? No — ADA requirements are legally mandated only in public accommodations and commercial facilities. Private residences are not required to meet ADA standards. However, the standards themselves are based on sound ergonomic and safety research, and applying them to a private bathroom results in a genuinely safer and more functional space. Some government assistance programs and VA grants require modifications to meet specific ADA or ANSI standards to qualify for reimbursement, so documentation of compliance can have financial value even in a residential setting. How much does an accessible bathroom remodel cost in Avondale? Cost depends heavily on scope. A focused accessibility upgrade — adding a roll-in shower conversion, installing compliant grab bars with proper backing, and replacing the toilet — might range from $8,000 to $18,000 depending on materials and structural needs. A comprehensive accessible bathroom remodel that includes widening doorways, installing a roll-under vanity, replacing all flooring, and fully restyling the space can range from $20,000 to $45,000 or more. The best way to get an accurate number for your specific project is a free in-home consultation — we measure, assess, and provide a detailed estimate with no obligation. Can grab bars be installed after the tile is done? Technically yes, but it is not ideal. Grab bars installed through finished tile into drywall alone cannot safely hold the required 250-lb load — the drywall will fail before the bar does. A proper installation requires the bar to be anchored into wall studs or into solid blocking (lumber or metal plate) installed between studs behind the wall surface. If blocking was not installed during the original construction or remodel, the wall must be opened to add it. This is one of the strongest arguments for planning accessible features before any tile work begins — it is straightforward to add blocking before the walls close up, and expensive to do so afterward. Will an accessible bathroom reduce my home's resale value? No — and for many buyers, it adds value. Aging-in-place features are actively sought by buyers who want a home they can stay in long-term without costly future renovations, and by families planning for a parent to move in with them. A curbless shower, comfort-height toilet, and well-placed grab bars are invisible to buyers who don't need them and highly valuable to buyers who do. The key is execution: an accessible bathroom that looks beautiful and is well-integrated into the home's design reads as a premium feature, not a limitation. That is exactly what Infinity Kitchens and Baths delivers. What are the key ADA bathroom dimensions? The three that matter most in a home are a 60-inch diameter turning space (§304.3.1), a 32-inch minimum clear width at doorways (§404.2.3), and grab bars set 33 to 36 inches above the finished floor (§609.4). We will tell you which of these your room can hit and which it cannot. What if my bathroom is too small to meet them? Most existing bathrooms are, and that is a normal starting point rather than a failure. We prioritise: doorway clear width first, then a curbless or low-threshold entry, then blocking and reach. A room that hits three of those is dramatically more usable than one that hits none while waiting for a full rebuild. What might you find behind the walls in an older Avondale home? Most often: supply lines that have narrowed with age, venting that no longer meets current code, blocking that is absent or in the wrong place, and evidence of an earlier remodel done without a permit . We check what we can before quoting and tell you what we would address while the wall is open, rather than tiling over it. Is testing for asbestos or lead necessary? In housing built before the late 1970s it is worth doing before demolition rather than during. Neither is present in every home, and a positive result is manageable — it means licensed abatement before we start, which adds time and cost. It is not something to find out about by cutting into it. Do I need a City of Avondale permit for an accessible bathroom remodel? Usually, yes. Avondale's code lets finish work such as tiling, cabinets and countertops go ahead without a building permit, but plumbing, electrical, gas and HVAC changes beyond minor repairs are not exempt — and moving a drain, recessing a floor for a curbless entry or reframing a doorway all fall into that category. Permits come from the city's Building Services Division, (623) 333-4000, and a rebuilt shower gets pre-slope and shower liner test inspections before tile goes on. We pull the permit and meet the inspector ourselves. If the project also includes an exterior ramp, check with your HOA first: the city does not track HOA rules. Vanity Countertop Materials The countertop you choose affects how your vanity looks, how it performs under daily moisture and cosmetics, and how much maintenance you&rsquo;ll be doing for years to come. In Avondale it also has to live with very hard water: the city&rsquo;s 2022 water quality report put city well water at about 21 grains per gallon — &ldquo;very hard&rdquo; on the report&rsquo;s own scale — and that leaves mineral rings around faucets and drains. We offer every major material and help you weigh the trade-offs honestly. Quartz Vanity Tops Engineered quartz is the most popular countertop material in bathroom vanities today, and for good reason. It is non-porous, which means no annual sealing and no concern about bacteria harboring in microscopic surface pores — a real advantage in a bathroom environment. Quartz holds up to acidic toiletry products, resists staining from makeup and hair dye, and is available in more than 100 colors and patterns, including convincing marble-look options that give you the luxurious aesthetic without the upkeep. Our quartz vanity tops are templated and fabricated specifically for your cabinet run, so overhangs, sink cutouts, and backsplash returns are all precise. Marble Vanity Tops Marble is the gold standard of bathroom luxury. The veining patterns are entirely natural — no two slabs are identical — and the depth of color in a polished Carrara or Calacatta slab is something engineered stone simply cannot fully replicate. Marble does require annual sealing and a bit more care to avoid etching from acidic products — and with hard water, from the mineral cleaners people reach for to remove spotting — but for homeowners who want a truly elevated primary bathroom, the investment is worth it. We arrange for you to see the actual slab before fabrication so you know exactly what your finished countertop will look like. Granite Vanity Tops Granite offers a natural stone option that sits between quartz and marble in terms of maintenance requirements. Each slab is unique, with movement and mineral patterns that give your vanity a one-of-a-kind appearance. Properly sealed granite is highly resistant to heat, scratches, and everyday bathroom use. It comes in a broader range of colors than marble — from classic white and cream tones to dramatic blacks, blues, and earth tones — making it a versatile choice for both traditional and contemporary bathroom designs. We can arrange slab viewing so you select your specific piece. Solid Surface / Corian Solid surface materials like Corian and similar brands are a practical, budget-conscious option that deserves more credit than it often receives. The key advantage is the ability to produce an integrated sink — the sink bowl and countertop are molded from a single continuous piece, eliminating the seam where most grime accumulates around undermount installations. Solid surface can also be routed to virtually any shape and is repairable if scratched. For aging-in-place and accessible bathroom projects, the seamless integrated sink option is especially useful. See Our Full Bathroom Remodeling Service Bathroom Vanity FAQ Common questions Avondale homeowners ask before getting started on a vanity project. How long does vanity installation take? A straightforward single-vanity swap — same footprint, no tile work, standard plumbing adjustment — typically takes one to two days from demo to finished plumbing. A double-vanity installation or one that involves wall blocking for a floating unit, new tile, or significant plumbing relocation may run two to four days. We provide a project-specific timeline at the estimate stage so you can plan accordingly. What&rsquo;s the best countertop material for a bathroom vanity? For most homeowners, engineered quartz is the easiest long-term choice because it requires no sealing and resists nearly everything a busy bathroom throws at it. If you want natural stone and are willing to seal it annually, marble gives an unmatched luxury look and granite offers similar durability with more color variety. For a budget-friendly option with an integrated sink, solid surface is worth a serious look. We walk through all the trade-offs during your consultation so you can choose based on your real lifestyle, not just aesthetics. Can I keep my existing plumbing with a new vanity? In many cases, yes — if the new vanity is the same width as the existing one and the sink is in the same general position, the existing supply lines and drain can often be reused or extended with minimal work. Where it gets more complicated is when you are switching from a single sink to a double vanity, changing from a floor-mounted to a wall-mounted unit, or significantly shifting the cabinet position. We assess your existing rough-in during the in-home consultation and give you a clear picture of what plumbing work, if any, will be required. What&rsquo;s the difference between a floating and a floor-mounted vanity? A floor-mounted (or freestanding) vanity sits on the bathroom floor with its cabinet box resting on the ground — the traditional configuration. A floating (wall-mounted) vanity is attached directly to wall studs or a reinforced substrate and hangs at a selected height with open floor space below it. Floating vanities give a cleaner, more contemporary look and make mopping the floor easier, but they do require proper structural support in the wall, which adds some labor cost. They also allow you to set the vanity height to your preference rather than accepting the standard 32-inch floor-mounted height. Do you install mirrors and medicine cabinets too? Yes — mirror and medicine cabinet installation is included as part of our vanity service. We can install a flat framed mirror, a frameless mirror, a single recessed medicine cabinet, or a full-width mirrored medicine cabinet depending on your preference and wall conditions. If a recessed unit is desired, we assess wall cavity depth and any obstructions before confirming feasibility. Coordinating the mirror or cabinet with your vanity and lighting is something we handle as part of the overall design process so everything looks intentional and cohesive. Do I need a permit to replace a bathroom vanity in Avondale? Not for the cabinet and countertop themselves — the City of Avondale&rsquo;s code lists cabinets and countertops as finish work that needs no building permit. Plumbing is different: moving supply or drain lines, adding a second sink, or replacing valves and fixtures falls outside the exemption and goes through the city&rsquo;s Building Services Division. We tell you at the consultation which side of that line your project falls on, and when a permit is needed we pull it and meet the inspector. Ready for a Vanity You&rsquo;ll Love Every Morning? How Groutless Systems Work Solid-Surface Panels — No Grout, No Mold, No Maintenance Groutless shower systems use thick acrylic or composite wall panels — typically 3/8" solid-surface material — that are bonded directly to your shower substrate and sealed at every seam. The result is a completely smooth, non-porous surface with zero grout lines. No places for water to pool, no crevices for soap scum to collect, and absolutely nowhere for mold or mildew to take hold. Traditional tile is beautiful, but grout is its Achilles heel. Within a year of installation, most homeowners find themselves scrubbing discolored grout lines, chasing mildew with bleach, and periodically hiring someone to re-caulk the corners. That cycle ends the moment you switch to a solid-surface panel system. A damp cloth and thirty seconds is genuinely all it takes to keep your shower spotless. In a tile shower those minerals settle into the grout joints as a white haze that stains light grout within months. On a solid-surface panel they sit on a non-porous face and wipe off. See the service Local Detail Why Avondale Changes the Shower Answer Hard water is the single biggest factor. Avondale's tap water is a blend of city well water and Colorado River water, and the city's 2022 water quality report put city well water at about 21 grains per gallon — "very hard" on the report's own scale. It leaves residue on every surface it dries on. In a shower, the first place that shows is the grout, because grout is porous and slightly recessed, followed closely by clear glass and polished chrome. This is why a shower that was beautiful for three years can start looking permanently dingy in year four, and why so many homeowners ask about groutless systems specifically. A whole-house softener helps too. The housing stock splits the decision too. Census figures put the median Avondale home's construction year at 2002, and about six in ten homes were built in the 1990s or 2000s. Most of those bathrooms still have a builder-grade tub/shower combination in an alcove, and those rooms convert beautifully — the alcove is already the right footprint for a walk-in shower, and the plumbing is usually where you need it. If your primary bath has both a garden tub and a small stall shower, combining the two into one larger walk-in is often the best use of the space. Older homes around Old Town and Cashion are a smaller share, and they are where we look hardest behind the walls. Heat and monsoon humidity. Avondale sits in the low desert at about 1,000 feet. National Weather Service 1991–2020 normals for the area put the July average high around 106&deg;F, and monsoon season runs June 15 to September 30. Bathrooms dry fast most of the year, but monsoon humidity is real and builder-grade exhaust fans are often undersized. We size the fan with the shower — see our ventilation and moisture guide . Permits and rebates. Tile on its own needs no building permit in Avondale, but replacing the valve, moving the drain or rebuilding the pan is plumbing work the City of Avondale's Building Services Division reviews, and its inspection list includes a pre-slope and shower liner test. We pull the permit and meet the inspector (our Avondale permit guide has the detail). And if you are on City water, the city's Low Flow Plumbing Rebate pays $25 per showerhead under 2.6 gallons per minute — apply within a year with a dated receipt, first come, first served; check the city's rebate page for current terms. And a practical note on scheduling: if the shower you are replacing is in the only full bathroom in the house, say so at the consult. It changes how we sequence the work, and in some cases it changes which wall system we recommend, because cure times differ. A full custom walk-in shower runs $10,000–$35,000 depending on size, wall material and whether the drain moves. Groutless solid-surface panels give you a shower with no grout lines to scrub, which matters a great deal in Avondale: the city's 2022 water quality report put city well water at about 21 grains per gallon, "very hard" on the report's own scale, and grout is where hard-water residue shows first. See curbless showers , ADA bathrooms and our aging-in-place work . Do I need to replace the shower or can it be refinished? If the tile is sound and only the grout has failed, a regrout is often enough — our shower grout guide has the diagnostic for telling the two apart. If water has gotten behind the wall, the substrate is soft, or you see movement in the tile, that is a rebuild. Home / Services / Bathroom Remodeling / Small Bathroom Remodeling Small Bathroom Remodeling Avondale, AZ Small Bathroom Remodeling in Avondale, AZ — Big Style, Small Space Maximize every inch of your compact bathroom with smart layouts, space-saving fixtures, and professional tile work. Small Bathroom Remodeling in Avondale Small Bathroom, Stunning Result The hall bathroom or guest bath is often the most-used room in an Avondale home. Avondale is a young, family-heavy city, and in a lot of houses the hall bath is the one the kids share. Visitors see it first. Family members use it every morning. Despite its size, it carries a disproportionate share of daily traffic — and daily frustration when the layout does not work. Cracked or stained grout, fixtures crusted with hard-water scale, a vanity that is too deep, and a door that swings into the toilet are all problems we hear about constantly from homeowners. Most small bathroom remodels fall short for the same reasons: the contractor chooses the wrong tile size, installs inadequate lighting, or ignores the storage plan entirely. A 4&times;6 bathroom with large-format floor tile in a dark grout, a single globe light, and no medicine cabinet will feel just as cramped after the remodel as before — sometimes more so. The work gets done, money gets spent, and the homeowner is left wondering why the room still feels small. At Infinity Kitchens and Baths, we solve that before demo day. Every small bathroom project starts with an in-home measurement at your Avondale home and a CAD layout so you can see exactly how the new shower, vanity, and fixtures will fit before we ever pick up a tool. That design-first approach is the same one we apply to every project in our full bathroom remodeling portfolio — and it is the difference between a bathroom that merely looks new and one that genuinely works better every day. Small Bathroom Design Strategies That Work Six proven techniques our design team uses on every compact bathroom project. Large Tile to Minimize Grout Lines A 12&times;24 or 24&times;24 floor tile creates far fewer grout lines than standard 4&times;4 or 6&times;6 tiles. Fewer lines mean the eye reads the floor as one continuous plane rather than a busy grid — making the entire room feel bigger without touching the walls. Floating Vanity A wall-mounted vanity exposes the floor beneath it, creating a visual line that extends across the room. That unbroken floor plane signals more square footage to the eye. Pair it with an under-vanity night light and the effect is even more dramatic in the morning. Walk-In Shower vs. Tub Removing an unused tub in a secondary bathroom can reclaim 15–18 square feet of usable floor space. A curbless walk-in shower also eliminates the visual barrier of a tub deck, making the room feel open from the doorway. Learn more about our tub-to-shower conversion service. Light Colors & Mirrors A white or cream tile palette reflects light rather than absorbing it. Combine that with a large frameless mirror — ideally spanning the full width of the vanity wall — and the perceived size of the room can nearly double. We often pair warm-white LED vanity lighting to reinforce the effect. Recessed Niches A tile-lined shower niche built between wall studs gives you shampoo and soap storage without adding a single protruding shelf. When the niche tile matches the surrounding wall tile, it blends in and adds storage without visual clutter — a technique we use on nearly every small shower project. Pocket Door or Barn Door A standard 2&rsquo;-6&rdquo; swing door requires a 7–10 square foot swing arc that you can never put furniture, a hamper, or a towel rack in. Replacing it with a pocket door or a sliding barn door reclaims that entire area for usable floor space and dramatically improves the flow of the room. Space-Saving Fixtures for Small Bathrooms The right fixtures can recover inches you did not know you had. Here is how we approach toilet and vanity selection for compact bathrooms. Compact & Wall-Hung Toilets Standard toilets measure about 30 inches from the wall to the front of the bowl. Compact elongated models bring that down to 27–28 inches — saving two to three inches in a room where every inch matters. Over the life of the bathroom you will appreciate that extra clearance every time you reach around the toilet to clean behind it or step out of the shower. Comfort height (17–19 inches to the seat) is easier on knees for most adults and is our most-requested toilet height. Standard height (15–16 inches) remains the right choice for households with children or homeowners with specific accessibility needs. For the ultimate space gain, a wall-hung toilet conceals the tank inside the wall cavity, reducing the toilet footprint to as little as 22 inches from wall to front of bowl and freeing floor space for cleaning. These require a proper carrier frame installed during the remodel — something we plan for during the CAD layout phase. If you are replacing a higher-use toilet or showerhead, check the City of Avondale&rsquo;s Low Flow Plumbing Rebate . It pays $75 per toilet (1.6 gallons per flush or less) and $25 per showerhead (under 2.6 gallons per minute) for City water customers replacing higher-use fixtures. Apply within a year with a dated receipt; funds are first come, first served, so check the city&rsquo;s page for current terms. We give you the model numbers and receipts you need. Vanity Options for Tight Spaces Standard vanities run 21 inches deep. When your bathroom is only 5 feet wide, that 21-inch vanity leaves just 39 inches of clear floor space — not enough to open a drawer and stand at the mirror comfortably. Narrow vanities at 18–19 inches deep solve that without sacrificing the sink bowl depth. A pedestal sink offers the most open floor space and the lowest price point, but provides zero storage. A floating vanity with drawers gives you storage plus the visual spaciousness of an open floor. For the smallest powder rooms where every inch counts, a vessel sink mounted on a narrow 18-inch shelf or floating vanity keeps the counter footprint minimal while still looking finished and intentional. Do not forget the medicine cabinet. Recessing a medicine cabinet into the wall above the vanity gives you a full mirror plus several inches of enclosed storage — without adding a single inch to the room. We routinely install medicine cabinets alongside custom bathroom vanities to maximize function in small spaces. Tile Choices That Make Small Bathrooms Feel Larger Tile selection in a small bathroom is not just aesthetic — it is a spatial design tool. The right tile size, orientation, and grout color can make a 5&times;8 bathroom feel like a 7&times;10 bathroom without moving a single wall. Floor Tile Size & Orientation Horizontal large-format tile laid on the floor in a landscape orientation visually elongates the room in its narrowest dimension. A 12&times;24 tile laid with the 24-inch dimension running across the short wall of a 5&times;8 bathroom makes the room read as wider than it is. A 24&times;24 tile works even better because there are essentially no grout lines from wall to wall. On the shower walls, vertical subway tile — classic 3&times;6 or larger 4&times;12 tiles set in a running bond — draws the eye upward and raises the perceived ceiling height. Extending the same floor tile or a complementary wall tile from the floor continuously up into the shower surround, with no color break at the threshold, removes the visual interruption that makes small bathrooms feel choppy. Our team handles all custom tile work in-house; see our tile shower installation service for details. Grout Color & Pattern Tips Grout color is one of the most overlooked decisions in a small bathroom remodel. Dark grout on a light tile creates a strong grid pattern that your eye traces from one side of the room to the other — making every grout line an interruption. Matching the grout color closely to the tile color (within two or three shades) causes the lines to nearly disappear, and the entire surface reads as a unified plane of color and texture. This is especially impactful on the floor. A large-format cream tile with ivory grout reads as a single continuous field. The same tile with dark charcoal grout looks like a checkerboard — and checkerboards are busy, not spacious. Epoxy grout has a further advantage in small, high-humidity bathrooms: it resists staining, does not require sealing, and holds its original color for years. That matters in Avondale, where tap water is a blend of city well water and Colorado River water and the city&rsquo;s 2022 water quality report put city well water at about 21 grains per gallon — &ldquo;very hard&rdquo; on the report&rsquo;s own scale. Cement grout picks up that mineral haze; epoxy shrugs it off. We use it on virtually every wet area we tile and recommend it for small bathroom floors where grout lines are closer together and see more cleaning traffic. Home / Guides / Shower & Tile Guides / Steam Shower Installation Bathroom Remodeling Guide — Avondale, AZ Steam Shower Installation: Cost & What to Know (Avondale, AZ) By Steve Hunt , Owner & Lead Designer at Infinity Kitchens and Baths Reviewed by Steve Hunt , Owner & Lead Designer &middot; AZ ROC #339999 Updated June 19, 2026 &bull; 6 min read Weighing shower types? Quick answer: A steam shower is a fully sealed, waterproof shower enclosure fitted with a steam generator. It requires a sealed ceiling (slightly sloped), a vapor-proof full-height door, non-porous walls (porcelain, stone, or solid surface), and meticulous waterproofing. Cost is a premium over a standard custom tile shower, driven by the generator plus the sealed enclosure. Infinity Kitchens and Baths (AZ ROC #339999) designs and builds steam showers in Avondale. A steam shower turns your daily shower into a spa experience — and it's one of the most-requested luxury upgrades we get asked about. But a steam shower is more than a fancy fixture; it's a fully sealed, purpose-built enclosure. Here's what to know before you commit. What Is a Steam Shower? A steam shower is an enclosed shower fitted with a steam generator that produces warm, moist vapor. Unlike a standard shower, the enclosure must be completely sealed — floor to ceiling — so the steam stays in and moisture doesn't damage the surrounding bathroom. What a Steam Shower Requires A fully sealed, waterproof enclosure — including a ceiling (sloped slightly so condensation runs off rather than dripping on you). A vapor-proof, full-height door with a transom or seal at the top. A steam generator sized to the enclosure's volume, usually installed nearby (a vanity cabinet, closet, or attic). Proper waterproofing behind every surface — steam finds any weakness in the system. Non-porous wall surfaces — porcelain tile, natural stone, or solid-surface panels. What Does a Steam Shower Cost? Cost depends on the size of the enclosure and the generator, plus the sealing and tile work involved. The steam generator itself is a meaningful line item on top of a standard custom shower build, and the fully sealed enclosure adds labor. We provide an exact figure after seeing your space; in general, a steam shower is a premium upgrade over a standard custom tile shower. Benefits Beyond pure relaxation, steam showers are valued for helping with congestion, sore muscles, and skin. They add a luxury, resort-like feature that stands out — and in our experience, the homeowners who add one rarely regret it. Things to Consider A steam shower must be enclosed (an open walk-in won't hold steam), and good bathroom ventilation outside the enclosure is important to manage overall humidity. The enclosure also needs to be built to handle constant moisture — which is exactly why waterproofing and the right materials matter so much. This is not a DIY or budget-contractor project. Steam Showers in Avondale: Hard Water, Heat and Permits Hard water. Avondale's tap water is a blend of city well water and Colorado River water, and the city's 2022 water quality report put city well water at about 21 grains per gallon — "very hard" on the report's own scale. A steam generator boils that water every time it runs, and the minerals stay behind as scale. We specify generators with an automatic drain or flush cycle, place them where they can be reached for descaling, and often recommend a water softener on the supply line. Generator location. The attic is a common spot for a generator, but Avondale attics get extremely hot: National Weather Service 1991–2020 normals for the area show roughly 111 days a year at 100&deg;F or hotter. We prefer a vanity cabinet, linen closet, or other conditioned space within the manufacturer's distance limit, so the unit stays cool and easy to service. Ventilation. Every session releases a cloud of moisture into the bathroom when the door opens, and monsoon season (June 15 – Sept. 30) brings humid, stormy weeks on top of that. A properly sized exhaust fan outside the enclosure, run after every use, keeps that moisture out of drywall and cabinets. Our guide to bathroom ventilation and moisture fixes covers fan sizing. Permits. A steam generator usually needs a new dedicated electrical circuit and a water supply, and the shower itself involves plumbing. In Avondale that work needs a permit from the City of Avondale's Building Services Division (Development Services Department, 11465 W. Civic Center Dr., 623-333-4000), filed online through Accela, and the city's inspection list includes a pre-slope and shower liner test before tile goes on. We pull the permit and meet the inspector. If you live in an HOA, check its rules as well — the city does not track HOA covenants. Our Avondale permit guide has more detail. Frequently Asked Questions How much does a steam shower cost? It's a premium upgrade over a standard custom tile shower . Cost depends on the enclosure size, the steam generator, and the sealing and tile work required. We give you an exact written estimate after evaluating your space. Can any shower be made into a steam shower? No — a steam shower must be a fully enclosed, sealed unit, including a sloped sealed ceiling and a vapor-proof door. An open or curbless walk-in shower won't hold steam. The enclosure must also be waterproofed to handle constant moisture. What surfaces work best in a steam shower? Non-porous materials: porcelain tile, natural stone (properly sealed), or solid-surface panels. The entire enclosure must be waterproofed behind the surface, since steam will find any weak point. Are steam showers worth it? For homeowners who want a spa-like experience, yes. They're prized for relaxation and for easing congestion and sore muscles, and they add a standout luxury feature. They do require a proper sealed build — this isn't a budget or DIY project. Do I need a permit for a steam shower in Avondale? In almost every case, yes. A steam generator usually needs a new dedicated electrical circuit and a water supply line, and the City of Avondale requires a permit for electrical and plumbing work beyond minor repairs. We pull the permit through the city's Building Services Division and meet the inspector, including the pre-slope and shower liner test before tile goes on. Tile Shower Installation Avondale, AZ Tile Work Done Right — Every Time Most shower failures don't start with the tile — they start with what's behind it. A beautiful tile shower is only as reliable as the waterproofing system underneath. When moisture finds its way through inadequate membrane work or poorly sealed grout lines, the damage spreads silently behind the walls, rotting substrate and driving up repair costs that dwarf the original installation. At Infinity Kitchens and Baths, waterproofing isn't an afterthought; it's the foundation every project is built on. What separates a professional tile installation from a cheap one comes down to the details most homeowners never see. Proper work means installing Schluter KERDI or equivalent uncoupling membranes, back-buttering every large-format tile to eliminate voids, maintaining precise slope toward the drain, and finishing every edge with Schluter trim profiles so corners stay clean and watertight for years. Skipping these steps produces a shower that looks fine on day one and starts leaking by year three. Infinity Kitchens and Baths brings that same level of craft to every tile shower we build in Avondale. Whether you're upgrading a dated tub surround, adding a custom steam shower, or building a brand-new bathroom remodel from the studs out, our tile crews handle the full scope — demo, substrate prep, waterproofing, layout, setting, grouting, and sealing — so you get a shower that looks exceptional and performs for decades. Tile Options for Your Custom Shower The tile you choose sets the tone for the entire bathroom. We work with every major tile category and help you find the material, size, and pattern that fits your design goals, your maintenance preferences, and your budget. In Avondale, factor in the water too: the city&rsquo;s tap water is a blend of city well water and Colorado River water, and its 2022 water quality report put city well water at about 21 grains per gallon — &ldquo;very hard&rdquo; on the report&rsquo;s own scale. That pushes most of our recommendations toward larger tiles with fewer joints and grout that resists mineral staining. Porcelain Tile The most popular choice for shower walls and floors. Porcelain is dense, low-absorption, and available in an enormous range of looks — from concrete and wood grain to classic stone. Because it absorbs so little, hard-water minerals stay on the surface where they wipe off rather than soaking in, and it requires minimal sealing compared to natural stone. Natural Stone (Travertine & Marble) Travertine and marble bring warmth and organic character that no manufactured tile can fully replicate. Both materials require proper sealing and periodic re-sealing to stay moisture-resistant, but when installed and maintained correctly they produce a timeless shower that adds genuine value to your home. With very hard water, plan on a daily squeegee: the acidic cleaners that dissolve mineral scale will etch marble and travertine. Large-Format Tile (24&times;48 and Beyond) Oversized tiles create a sleek, contemporary look with fewer grout lines, meaning less maintenance and a more expansive feel in any shower size. Large-format installation demands a perfectly flat substrate, back-buttering to achieve full coverage, and careful layout planning to avoid awkward cuts — all skills our crew practices on every job. Subway Tile & Classic Patterns The 3&times;6 subway tile earned its place as a classic because it works in virtually any design. Stack bond, herringbone, offset, or vertical — the pattern you choose transforms the same tile into a completely different aesthetic. We help you visualize layouts during the design consultation so there are no surprises on installation day. Mosaic & Accent Tile Glass, ceramic, and stone mosaics work beautifully as shower floor surfaces, decorative border bands, or full accent walls behind a showerhead. The smaller format gives them natural flexibility around curves and niches. We incorporate mosaic accents strategically so they elevate the design without overwhelming it. Pebble & Natural River Stone Pebble floors add a spa-like texture underfoot and pair well with both contemporary and natural design themes. Because pebble tile has more grout surface area than most options, sealing and proper slope are critical. We ensure every pebble floor is fully sealed and pitched correctly so water doesn't pool between the stones. Large-format tiles are back-buttered for complete mortar coverage; mosaic sheets are pressed firmly into the thinset bed. After the thinset cures, joints are grouted with the specified product, then carefully cleaned and finished. Schluter edge profiles are set at all exposed tile edges for a polished, professional look that also protects the corners from chipping. 05 Sealing, Fixtures & Final Walkthrough Once the grout has fully cured, we apply a penetrating sealer to the tile and grout surfaces. Explore Full Bathroom Remodeling Tile Shower Installation FAQ Common questions from Avondale homeowners planning a tile shower project. How long does tile shower installation take? A standard tile shower replacement — demo, waterproofing, tile, grout, and fixtures — typically takes 5 to 8 business days depending on the size and complexity of the space. Projects that include significant framing repairs, custom niches, or large-format tile requiring extended mortar cure times may run closer to two weeks. We provide a realistic schedule during the design consultation so you can plan accordingly. What size tile works best in a shower? There's no single right answer — it depends on your aesthetic goals and shower dimensions. Large-format tiles (12&times;24 and up) minimize grout lines and feel expansive in any size shower. Smaller tiles like 4&times;4 or 3&times;6 subway are easier to work around curves and niches. For shower floors, tiles smaller than 4&times;4 are generally recommended because more grout lines mean more texture and grip underfoot, which improves safety on a wet surface. Do I need to waterproof before tiling? Yes — absolutely and without exception. Tile and grout are not waterproof; they are water-resistant at best. Without a dedicated waterproofing membrane behind the tile, moisture will eventually penetrate grout lines and reach the substrate, leading to mold, rot, and structural damage. We use Schluter KERDI membrane on every tile shower we build, regardless of tile type or project budget. How do I keep my grout from molding? Proper sealing at installation is the foundation — we apply a penetrating grout sealer after full cure. Beyond that, the best long-term habits are keeping grout sealed on an annual basis (most sealers last 1–2 years in shower environments), running your bathroom exhaust fan during and after every shower, and squeegeeing shower walls after use to reduce standing moisture. Epoxy grout is a zero-maintenance alternative worth considering if you want to minimize grout care entirely, and with Avondale's very hard water it also resists the mineral staining that discolors light cement grout. Can you match existing tile in my bathroom? We do our best to match tile when the goal is blending a repair with existing work. However, exact matches are often difficult because tile dye lots vary between production runs, and discontinued patterns may no longer be available from manufacturers. In many cases, homeowners find this is a good opportunity to update the entire shower or floor with a coordinated new look. We'll give you an honest assessment during the consultation and show you comparable options if an exact match isn't achievable. Do I need a permit for a new tile shower in Avondale? It depends on what changes behind the tile. The City of Avondale's code exempts tiling and similar finish work from a building permit, but replacing or moving the shower valve, drain or supply pipes is plumbing work that is not exempt. Those permits come from the city's Building Services Division (Development Services Department, 11465 W. Civic Center Dr., 623-333-4000) and are filed online through Accela, and the city's inspection list includes a pre-slope and shower liner test before tile goes on. We pull the permit and meet the inspector. If you live in an HOA, check its rules too, because the city does not track HOA covenants. Start Your Project Ready for a Shower That Looks Incredible? See All Bathroom Services Cast iron, and what it means for an Avondale conversion Most Avondale homes were built in the 1990s and 2000s, and in those houses the tub is usually a lighter builder-grade unit that comes out quickly. Older homes are different. Around Old Town and Cashion the tub may well be cast iron, and a five-foot cast iron tub weighs enough that removing it whole is frequently impossible through a standard doorway. The usual answer is to break it up in place, which is loud, messy, and requires protecting everything between the bathroom and the door. That is a real line item and an honest contractor will say so. It is not a reason to avoid the conversion — it is a reason the conversion in a 1960s house costs more than the identical conversion in a 2005 house, and a quote that prices them the same has not looked at your tub. What you get in exchange is usually a better wall to build on. Older framing is often full-dimension lumber, and once the tub is gone there is real material to fasten blocking to. The plumbing behind an older alcove The other variable is what the supply and waste are made of. In a 2000s tract home the answer is usually unremarkable. In an older house, galvanized supply that has been in the wall for decades narrows from the inside, and you often only discover how badly when the new shower runs at half the pressure the old tub did. Because the wall is already open for the conversion, this is the cheapest moment in the life of the house to address it. We will tell you what we find and what we would do, and we will not quietly tile over a problem to keep a number down. Venting is the same story. Older bathrooms were sometimes vented in ways that no longer meet code, and a conversion that changes the drain is exactly the point at which an inspector will look at it. While the valve and showerhead are being replaced anyway, it is worth knowing that the City of Avondale's Low Flow Plumbing Rebate pays $25 per showerhead (under 2.6 gallons per minute) and $75 per toilet (1.6 gallons per flush or less) for City water customers replacing higher-use fixtures. Apply within a year with a dated receipt; funds are first come, first served, so check the city's rebate programs page for current terms. Asbestos, lead, and the tests worth doing first Only a small share of Avondale's homes were built before 1980, but if yours is one of them, two things are worth checking before demolition rather than during it: asbestos in sheet flooring, mastic or joint compound, and lead in older paint layers. Neither is common in every house and neither is a reason to abandon a project. Both are a reason not to have a crew put a reciprocating saw through a wall on the assumption it will be fine. Testing is inexpensive relative to the cost of handling a positive result badly, and a contractor who waves the question away is telling you how they handle the things they cannot see. Where a test comes back positive, the work is done by a licensed abatement contractor before we start. That adds time and cost, and it is not optional. Here's what's included in every project: &#10003; Custom shower pan or mud-bed base — sloped correctly to the drain, with no low spots that let water pool and degrade the substrate over time. &#10003; Large-format tile walls — from 12&times;24 up to 24&times;48 porcelain and natural stone, set plumb and level with consistent grout joints throughout. &#10003; Frameless or semi-frameless glass door — heavy-duty tempered glass, properly plumbed and sealed, with your choice of hardware finish. &#10003; Rainfall and handheld showerheads — dual-function shower systems are standard on most builds; we also wire in thermostatic valve systems on request. &#10003; Built-in bench or recessed niche — tiled-in bench seating and shampoo niches are framed and waterproofed as part of the shower structure, not added as afterthoughts. &#10003; Waterproofing membrane system — Schluter Kerdi or RedGard membrane applied behind tile walls and under the floor pan for a fully sealed, moisture-proof shower envelope. &#10003; Proper slope and drainage engineering — every floor is sloped to specification so water drains fully with no standing water, reducing mold risk and extending the life of the installation. &#10003; Epoxy grout or caulk-free sealing options — we offer stain-resistant epoxy grout and grout-free panel systems for homeowners who want a lower-maintenance finished surface. Why Waterproofing Matters More Than Tile Dry desert air doesn't save a badly built shower. A shower that isn't properly waterproofed will fail — it's a matter of when, not if. Water finds its way through grout joints and caulk lines, and once it reaches the substrate it causes dry rot, mold, and structural damage that can cost far more to remediate than the original remodel. We use a redundant waterproofing approach: cement board or Schluter board substrate, full membrane application at seams and corners, a properly sloped mortar bed, and seam-sealed glass installation. The tile is the beautiful part. The membrane is what makes it last. A standard walk-in shower has a low curb or threshold — typically two to four inches high — at the entry point. The curb contains water and is simple to construct because the shower floor is elevated above the bathroom floor. A curbless or barrier-free shower has no threshold at all: you step directly from the bathroom floor into the shower without stepping up or over anything. Curbless showers require a more complex installation because the shower floor must be precisely sloped to a linear or point drain, and the surrounding bathroom floor must transition cleanly. They're ideal for aging-in-place accessibility and for a seamless modern aesthetic, and they're one of our most requested shower styles. Our curbless shower guide covers the details.
